prompt:
A design-sprint storyboard drawn in Copic markers and black fineliner on white marker paper: three panels in a row, each with a short hand-lettered caption underneath. Panel 1: At home, a traveller switches between notes, maps and booking pages. Screen text: "Where do I start?" Caption: Planning is spread across too many places. Panel 2: On a phone, the traveller answers a few questions and sees transport, places and tasks together. Screen text: "Build my China plan" Caption: Their answers shape one connected plan. Panel 3: At the airport, the traveller checks the same plan before boarding. Screen text: "Today in China" Caption: The trip is easier to follow.
Style: mostly white paper showing through, with light cool grey marker shading only where needed to separate planes — keep it airy. One warm orange accent on the key screen elements. Loose confident linework, a few visible marker streaks but not filled in. People are simple sketched figures with no facial detail. Any text on a screen, card or sign is short, legible and spelled exactly as given; captions are hand-lettered in neat block capitals. Feels like a real concept storyboard stuck on a workshop wall. No logos, no brand names, no watermark. The three panels and their captions fill the frame edge to edge, with only a slim paper margin.
